newsitem.title: UK: UK Aug consumer industry indicator at record high.
newsitem.headline: UK Aug consumer industry indicator at record high.

text.p: Britain's consumer industries' leading indicator rose to another record high in August, to 106.85 from 106.07 in July, NTC Research said on Thursday.
This is the third consectutive month in which a record high has been reached.
"The steady rise in the indicator over the past year therefore points to an acceleration in the rate of economic growth from mid-1996 to mid-1997," NTC said.
The indicator is compiled from a broad range of variables and NTC said it tends to move in advance of the cycle by around one year.

Five key factors have driven the recent performance of the indicator. They are tighter labour market conditions, low interest rates, improved consumer confidence, strong growth in television advertising expenditure and further growth in the output of consumer goods industries.

NTC also published its inflation indicator this month which showed the rate of underlying inflation was set to remain subdued this year and next, but faster economic growth was likely to translate into higher inflation beyond this period. It signals a rise in inflation excluding home loan costs throughout 1998, reaching 5.0 percent at the end of the year.
NTC has been calculating the inflation indicator for the last 18 months but said it has had a good track record in predicting turning points in inflation since 1967 if back data are used.
NTC is an independent research group which also compiles the UK Purchasing Managers Index.
